data_scene_asset_lists:
Scene asset lists: 98 records, one per scene, with the load commands of each scene (file offsets 163840-167937, SNES $05:8000-$9001, bank 02; 4098 bytes).

=== MODEL ===
LoadSceneAssets (lib_scene_asset_loader) calls FindSceneRecord to find the record of area_current and scene_current in this list (dp$2F-$31 points at it) and runs its commands: graphics, palette, tileset, tilemap, asset8 (scene profile or jump), meta4, music and spritemap, each with its operand bytes, ending with a 00 byte. The layout of the commands and the shared segments (65 jumps to 37 labels) are the subject of the block note of lib_scene_asset_loader.
Counts over the whole list: 47 spritemap, 65 music, 200 asset8, 135 tilemap, 62 tileset, 109 palette and 107 graphics commands, none of meta4. The first record (area $53, scene $59) is a dummy without commands; the other 97 are exactly the 97 scenes of ScenePlacementIndex. The list has no end sentinel (OQ-I011-3).
lib_02719F:
Boot-time expansion of three graphics blocks into fixed WRAM buffers (file offsets 160159-160290, SNES $04:F19F-$F222, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
LoadBootGraphicsBuffers decompresses graphics_054000 ($4000 bytes), graphics_05C000 and graphics_04D000 ($2000 bytes each) with DecompressQuintetLz into the scratch area $7E:8000 and moves each result with MVN #$7F,#$7E to its buffer: $7F:3000, $7F:1000 and $7F:C000. The source pointer in dp$29-$2B skips the 2-byte length header of each block (+2); dp$23 is the output length and dp$25 the destination offset. It ends with ResetSortBuckets, so the actor sort buckets start empty.

=== NOTES ===
- The only caller is the boot actor of the front end (code_0066DE in gv_front_end), once per start-up, after the SPC upload and RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette; it then jumps to the title scene with COP [10].
- The consumers are elsewhere: QueueAnimatedTileStrip reads its strips from $7F:1000 (frame x $80), the equipment menu copies $7F:C000 to VRAM word $2000 (RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette), and the engine's initial dynamic-tile pointer $1A02/$1A04 is $7F:3000 (InitFixedState; BuildDynamicTileSprites overwrites it before reading it, static reading). What graphics_054000 holds is open; this routine only places it.
- $7E:8000 is also the BG1 id map of the field; the buffer is free at boot and rebuilt by the first scene load.
lib_027223:
Request of the animated background tile strip and its four VRAM destinations (file offsets 160291-160351, SNES $04:F223-$F25F, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
Once per frame QueueAnimatedTileStrip prepares one strip for the NMI: vram_strip_src = $1000 + (frame_counter & $1F) x $80 (a source frame in the buffer at $7F:1000, 32 frames of $80 bytes), vram_strip_dest = AnimatedStripVramDests[frame_counter & 3] and vram_strip_pending is incremented. DmaAnimatedTileStrip (engine_vblank_nmi) then copies $40 bytes to the destination and the next $40 bytes to the destination + $100 words.
So each of the four VRAM slots is refreshed every 4 frames, and each slot cycles through 8 of the 32 source frames. The destinations $2060, $2080, $20A0, $20C0 are 16-word (4bpp) tiles $206, $208, $20A, $20C; the second half lands one tile row (16 tiles) lower, so a slot is a 2 x 2 tile block (OQ-I013-14: which tiles the maps use).

=== NOTES ===
- Skipped in locations $0F-$12 (location_id - $0F below 4), the same locations that have no HUD.
- It has no loop guard: it overwrites the three variables on every call, so five calls in one frame (the main loop and four wait loops of the front end) change nothing.
lib_027277:
Sine wave tables for an HDMA effect, unused (file offsets 160375-160439, SNES $04:F277-$F2B7, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
FillSineWaveTables is a request-driven table builder: when wave_request ($03CD) is non-zero it clears it and writes 256 words amplitude x sin(phase), using the hardware multiplier (M7A, M7B, MPYM), twice, to $7E:7900 and $7E:7B00. The sine byte comes from SineTable (a signed table in data_engine_tables); the phase starts at 0 and advances by wave_phase_step ($03CE) per word; wave_amplitude ($03CC) is the multiplier (one byte, M7A written twice with its second write 0).

=== NOTES ===
- Dead code: no routine calls it (OQ-I013-12) and the three parameter cells $03CC-$03CE have no other user (searched in the extracted sources). The tables $7E:7900 and $7E:7B00 sit in the area the HDMA staging uses ($7E:7000-$7BFF, left unnamed in docs/wram-memory-map.md); no other reader of the two addresses was checked here.
- The mnemonics wave_amplitude, wave_request and wave_phase_step name the cells from this routine only (confidence C).
lib_027572:
Pause with the location banner (file offsets 161138-161260, SNES $04:F572-$F5EC, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
HandlePauseBanner is called once per frame from RunMainLoop (after the field buttons). It is a latch: pause_latch ($03A2) negative = return; non-zero = Start was already handled, return while Start is still held and clear the latch when it is released; zero and Start newly pressed (joy_pressed+1 bit $10) = pause.
A pause runs inside the routine: it sets the latch, writes $F2 to APUIO0 (a request to the sound driver, OQ-I013-6), prints the location name (LocationBannerText) and, when no_combat_scene is clear, the lair counter (lairs_left as two BCD digits at $1B80 through ByteToPackedBcd, then LairCounterText), flushes the text with vram_upload_flags = 1, waits until Start is released and then pressed again (WaitFrameForStart each frame), prints PauseCloseText to erase the text (OQ-I013-10), writes $01 to APUIO0 and returns. The banner is skipped when the A button is held at the moment of pausing (JOY1L bit 7, OQ-I013-7): the game still pauses, without text.
WaitFrameForStart decrements frame_counter before it waits one vblank. The NMI increments it every frame, so the net change is 0: the game clock stands still during the pause.

=== NOTES ===
- Walkthrough 01-in-the-beginning.md: the number of lairs in the area is shown by pressing Start.
- pause_latch stays 1 after the resume until Start is let go, so the Start that ends the pause does not start a new one.
lib_027781_part1:
Player pose after a scene load or the equipment menu (file offsets 160761-160865, SNES $04:F3F9-$F461, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
ApplyPlayerWeaponPose chooses between two animation sets of the player: the unarmed one when no_combat_scene ($0439) is non-zero or no weapon is equipped (equipped_weapon $1B5E = 0), the armed one otherwise. Actor field $24 is the animation data bank of an actor (lib_animation): the unarmed pose sets it to $0A, the armed one to $0B (the normal player bank, the comment in the player code says $0B).
Unarmed: $1E = PlayerFacingByAnim[old $1E] xor 1 (the standing animation id for the current facing), $20 = 0, SetActorAnimFrame, and the weapon actor ($039E) gets bit $2000 of $16 set (hidden). Armed: $20 = 0, SetActorAnimFrame, weapon actor bit $2000 cleared; $1E is kept.
It does nothing in locations $0F-$12 (location_id - $0F below 4).

=== NOTES ===
- Callers: the end of InitSceneState (after the two RunActors passes) and ExitEquipmentMenu in lib_menus, where a weapon change must show at once.
- What bank $0A contains (a sword-less set?) is not verified (OQ-I031-3).
lib_027912:
Fixed engine state and new-game starting values, set once at reset (file offsets 162066-162228, SNES $04:F912-$F9B4, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
InitFixedState stores the layer parameters the loaders and the streaming code read (map bases $8000 and $C000, tilemap VRAM $6000 and $7000, tile definitions $2000 and $2800, strip work areas $3000, $3102, $3204, $3306), the bank bytes $7E of the strip pointers in dp$34, $37 and $2E, the RAM copy stub at $1C5C, text_delay = 3, a dynamic-tile source pointer, and the starting game values: event flag $FF set (the word $1A7D = $0080), HP and max HP 8, level 1 (also the BCD level), and the initial lair_state of every lair from the 32-byte records of LairRecords (byte +$13).
The RAM stub is PHB, MVN src,dst, PLB, RTS (8B 54 xx xx AB 60) at $1C5C; CopyFrameData patches the two bank operands and jumps to it (wram_copy_stub), because MVN has its banks in the instruction.

=== NOTES ===
- Called once from BootGame in engine_boot_main_loop, before the first scene loads, so a loaded save overwrites the starting values and a new game keeps them.
- Event flag $FF (bit 7 of $1A7D) is set here at every start-up and travels with the save image. This is the writer OQ-I011-13 looked for: the 13 unk13 map-patch rows that test flag $00FF see it set (answers the 'who sets it' part; whether it is ever cleared is open).
- $1A02/$1A04 are the long pointer of the dynamic-tile sprite code (BuildDynamicTileSprites builds it from actor $34/$2C before it reads it); the initial $7F:3000 is the buffer LoadBootGraphicsBuffers fills with graphics_054000. A read before the first write was not found.
lib_bit_array:
Set, clear and test of one bit in a bit array (file offsets 160584-160723, SNES $04:F348-$F3D3, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
Three routines share one addressing rule: A = bit number (& $3FF, at most 1024 bits), Y = address of the array. The byte is Y + ((A & $3F8) >> 3) and the mask comes from SwitchBitMasks (01 02 04 08 10 20 40 80) indexed by A & 7. All three save A, X, Y and P; TestBitInArray returns the result in the carry (set = the bit is set).
The arrays the callers pass in Y: $1A7E chests opened (bit = chest id & $7F), $1A9E lairs released (bit = lair index), $1ADE switches set (bit = switch id); $1A5E is event_flags, and the arrays at $1A7E, $1A9E and $1ADE lie inside the range that holds the event flags and the saved progress image ($1A5E-$1C57).

=== NOTES ===
- Callers: SetBitInArray 7 sites (lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return 5, engine_003005 2), TestBitInArray 11 sites (lib_scene_map_patches 5, cop_script_flow_flags 3, lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return 2, engine_003005 1).
- ClearBitInArray has no caller (OQ-I013-12).
lib_map_index_helpers:
Pixel position to map index conversion, the two index steppers and the metatile hazard test (file offsets 160440-160583 and 160866-161137, SNES $04:F2B8-$F347 and $F462-$F571, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
The field maps are stored as 256-byte pages of 16 x 16 metatiles (one byte per 16 x 16 pixel metatile), pages in rows of map_width_pages. PixelToMapIndex turns the pixel position in dp$16 (x) and dp$18 (y) into the byte index: index = ((map_width_pages x (y >> 8) + (x >> 8)) << 8) + y_low + ((x >> 4) & $0F), with 8-bit adds for the page byte and the low byte; an index of $4000 or more (a map of at most 64 pages) returns 0. The index is the same for every map-sized array: the BG1 id map $7E:8000, the BG2 map $7E:C000 and tile_type_map ($7F:8000).
y_low is added as it is, without masking its low nibble: the exact row-major index needs y with a low nibble of 0, otherwise the low nibble is added to the column (OQ-I031-1). IsPlayerOnMetatile masks y before it calls.
StepMapIndexEast moves the index one metatile to the east (+1, or +$F1 in the last column of a page to reach column 0 of the next page); StepMapIndexSouth one metatile to the south (+$10 on the low byte; at the end of a page the carry adds map_width_px, the next page row). PixelToBg1VramAddr is different: it turns the pixel position into the VRAM word address of the 8 x 8 tile in the BG1 tilemap at $6000, a 64 x 64 tile map made of four 32 x 32 screens (x bit 8 adds $400, y bit 8 adds $800).
IsPlayerOnMetatile tests whether the BG1 id at the player's feet row (y - $10: y is the bottom edge of the actor) is a given id, over the 1, 2 or 4 metatiles the player's 16-pixel box covers: x and y multiples of 16 = 1 cell, only x = 2 cells one below the other, only y = 2 cells side by side, neither = 4 cells (walked east, south, east). It returns carry set at once for a cell that matches, and carry clear at once when the player's flags have $0C00 (hit stun $0800 or dying $0400).

=== NOTES ===
- PixelToMapIndex has about 40 callers (player_core, cop_core, cop_tiles_spawn_kill, lib_scene_map_patches, lib_0108BB, lib_0109D6_part1, lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return, lib_menus, engine_spawn_lairs_death_drops and four actor files); it needs M = 16 on entry and returns with M = 16 (it ends with REP #$20). It relies on B holding the high byte of dp$18 after LDA $18 at M = 16 (the page row for Multiply8x8).
- IsPlayerOnMetatile is the floor hazard of four scenes. Each script first tests an inventory entry with Cop19 and only checks the tile while the item is not worn, then hurts the player with Cop39: Lostside Marsh id $80, 1 damage (guarded by item entry $0A; walkthrough items.md: Ice Armor protects from the fiery floors in Lostside), Leo's Laboratory dungeon ids $F3 and $E1, 4 damage (item entry $0A; 06-dr-leos-lab.md: equip the Ice Armor for the flaming bridges), Magridd's Castle dungeon id $88, 3 damage (item entry $0F; walkthrough items.md: Elemental Mail prevents spike damage), and the St. Elles coast id $47, 4 damage (after a COP [07] flag test; what the tile is is open, OQ-I031-2).
- The routine never saves P: M = 16 is an input and kept on return.
lib_player_facing:
Facing code of the player and the horizontal flip of an actor (file offsets 160724-160760, SNES $04:F3D4-$F3F8, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
GetPlayerFacing reads the player's animation id (actor $1E) and returns the facing code PlayerFacingByAnim[id] (a 44-byte table in data_engine_tables, ids $00-$2B): 0 up, 1 down, 2 right, 3 left (the probe points of RunTalkInteraction, OQ-I009-7). Animation ids of $2C or more have no facing: carry set. The animation id is read as a word, so $1F must be 0.
FlipActorX toggles bit $4000 of the actor's $1C word, the horizontal flip flag.

=== NOTES ===
- Callers: RunTalkInteraction (lib_menus) for the probe point of the talk button and TryOpenChest (lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return); ChooseFacingAnim (lib_menus) calls FlipActorX to show an NPC's side view mirrored.
- ApplyPlayerWeaponPose reads the same table and xors the code with 1 to get the standing animation id of the unarmed set.
lib_player_stats:
Pay-out of pending heal and EXP, and the EXP and Gem counters (file offsets 161261-161517, SNES $04:F5ED-$F6ED, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
heal_pending ($043B) and exp_pending ($043D) are queues that Cop37_HealPlayerToFull and Cop38_QueueExp fill; UpdateHud calls DrainPendingHeal and DrainPendingExp once per frame (not in locations $0F-$12) and the drains pay them out slowly so the HUD animates. All counters are BCD (decimal mode).
DrainPendingHeal: every 4th frame (frame_counter & 3 = 0) heal_pending - 1 and player_hp + 1 with BRK #$48 (OQ-I013-5); when HP is already at player_max_hp the rest of heal_pending is dropped. hud_dirty_flags bit $04 redraws the HP bar.
DrainPendingExp: every 8th frame, with BRK #$48, it takes one unit of the lowest non-zero BCD digit of exp_pending (ones, then tens, then hundreds, then thousands), subtracts it from exp_pending and calls AddExp with it; hud_dirty_flags bit $02 redraws the EXP. A pending 0132 pays 1, 1, 10, 10, 10, 100 in six steps.
AddExp: player_exp ($1B78, low word) and player_exp+2 ($1B7A, high word) are one eight-digit BCD number; on a carry out of the high word both words are set to $9999, so EXP maxes at 99,999,999 (walkthrough level-up.md agrees). AddGems: gems_low ($1B66) + A with the carry into gems_high ($1B68); gems_high can be at most $0099, so a carry ($0100, >= $009A) caps both at 999,999 (OQ-I013-8: the walkthrough gives no Gem cap). SubtractGems takes A from the Gems and returns carry set when there are not enough (nothing is taken).

=== NOTES ===
- Callers: AddExp from DrainPendingExp and from the two kill paths of engine_scheduler_sprites_combat_collision (KillTarget and the second kill path at loc_000CFC: the EXP of the meta entry, +3, is added at once, not through exp_pending). Cop36_AddExp (0 uses) does its own decimal add and does not call AddExp. AddGems: ApplyGemPickup, the chest code (TryOpenChest) and Cop25_AddGems (0 uses). SubtractGems: Cop26_PayGemsOrJump.
- DrainPendingHeal and DrainPendingExp run with M = 8; AddExp, AddGems and SubtractGems with M = 16. All routines leave the decimal flag clear.
- docs/wram-memory-map.md said player_exp is 24-bit BCD; the code and the walkthrough make it eight digits (four bytes $1B78-$1B7B, followed by player_exp_next at $1B7C), corrected in the same step (OQ-I031-4).
lib_save_system:
Save and load of the four save slots in SRAM, with the checksum that guards them (file offsets 159972-160158, SNES $04:F0E4-$F19E, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
A slot is a $400-byte block at $70:slot x $400 (slot 0-3). The same image is kept a second time at +$1000, the backup mirror, and the word $70:1FFE is the last used slot.
Layout of one slot: +$000 lair_state ($200 bytes, copied from $7F:0203); +$200 the progress image $1A5E-$1C57 ($1FA bytes: event_flags, Gems, level, EXP, HP, equipment, inventory, the player name at $1B92 = slot offset $334, saved_scene at $1B90); +$3FA the checksum sum word; +$3FC the checksum xor word.
Checksum: both words start at $3652; for each of the first $1FD words of the slot the sum word adds it (16-bit wrap) and the xor word xors it. So the two stored words are not part of the checksum. A slot is valid when both stored words equal the recomputed ones.
Save order: SaveGameToSlot first stores saved_scene ($1B90) = world_index + 1 into the live image (so it is saved too), then save_slot into $70:1FFE, copies lair_state and the image, stores the checksum and mirrors the slot ($3FE bytes, which include the checksum words) to +$1000. LoadGameFromSlot validates the main copy only: repairing a damaged main copy from the mirror is the job of the file select (DrawSaveSlotMenu in engine_title_file_select), which also refreshes the mirror.

=== NOTES ===
- Callers: the Master's record question (code_0076EF in shared_actor_helpers_bank0, after the answer Yes) calls SaveGameToSlot; the file select (engine_title_file_select) calls LoadGameFromSlot and ComputeSlotChecksum.
- saved_scene = world_index + 1 is the scene of area 0 the file select loads after Continue: scene 1 to 7 of Up Above are the shrines of the worlds in world order (docs/areas-and-scenes.md). The walkthrough describes saving at the Master's Shrine (06-dr-leos-lab.md, 'go there to heal and save').
- All three routines are JSL and need 16-bit index registers (LDX #$0203); X is preserved, DBR and P are restored.
lib_scene_change_init:
Scene change: the loader, the transitions, the iris, the tile type map and the scene state init (file offsets 161518-162065 and 162229-162514, SNES $04:F6EE-$F911 and $F9B5-$FAD2, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
ChangeSceneIfRequested is the scene loader called from RunMainLoop (and once at boot). It acts only when the low byte of scene_next ($0318) is non-zero. With scene_active set it first plays PlayTransitionOut with iris_frame = $1E and iris_step = $FF (the out direction of the iris); then it clears scene_active and dp$42, forces blank with the NMI off, copies scene_next and area_next into scene_current and area_current, clears scene_next, runs InitSceneState and one RunSubFrameLoader, enables the NMI, sets iris_frame = 0 and iris_step = 1, plays PlayTransitionIn, sets scene_active, clears transition_type and scene_loading and runs one more sub-frame. At boot scene_active is 0 and the out transition is skipped.
transition_type ($03E3, set by Cop3C_SetTransitionType; RunReturnLoop writes $80) selects the effect. Out: 0 and 1 fade, 2 and 3 instant, 4 and 5 mosaic, 6 and 7 instant, 8-$7F fade, $80 and above iris. In: 0 fade, 1 instant, 2 fade, 3 instant, 4 mosaic, 5 instant, 6 mosaic, 7 instant, 8-$7F fade, $80 and above iris. The type is cleared only after the in transition, so one type drives both halves of a scene change. The values in use are few: 0 (the default, fade out and fade in), 4 (set by 23 scripts through Cop3C, always just before a Cop10: mosaic out and mosaic in) and $80 (return trips: iris out and iris in); the other ladder entries are never selected by a script (static, OQ-I031-6). Fade = INIDISP brightness $0F down to 0 (out) or 0 up to $0F (in), one sub-frame per step; instant = one sub-frame, then INIDISP 0 or $0F; mosaic = two sub-frames per brightness step with MOSAIC = ((brightness xor $0F) << 4) | 3 (BG1 and BG2), 16 steps.
The iris (RunIrisTransition) writes one 16-byte frame of IrisFrames to VRAM word $4000 per step (the mask tile) and runs two sub-frames. The frame offset is ((2 x type + bit 4 of iris_frame) << 8) | ((iris_frame & $0F) << 4), the type's bit 7 drops out of the 8-bit add. iris_step is $FF for out (frames $1E down to 0, 31 steps = 62 sub-frames) and 1 for in (frames 0 up to $1F, 32 steps = 64 sub-frames). Out sets scene_loading, clears the BG3 buffer and sets vram_upload_flags bit 0 first.
BuildTileTypeMap fills tile_type_map ($7F:8000, one byte per metatile, OQ-I013-2) when a scene loads: FillTileTypeMap first builds a mask table at $0200-$02FF from the metatile definitions at $7E:2000 (8 bytes per metatile id = four tile words TL, TR, BL, BR): mask = TL + 2 TR + 4 BL + 8 BR where each term is bit 9 of the tile word (the solid flag; the same rule SetMetatileBg1 uses); then it replaces every id byte of the BG1 id map ($7E:8000) by mask[id]. The byte count is map_width_pages x map_height_pages x $100; the XBA/TAY that makes it is right only while the product fits one byte, and the largest header is 64 pages.
InitSceneState runs with the screen blanked and the NMI off. In order: zero player_x and player_y, the scroll deltas, joy_pressed, $03D4-$03D8, the BG2 offsets, joy_block_mask, $0433 (stored twice, OQ-I013-13), boss_fight_active, player_hidden_count and joy_override; weapon actor, soul orb actor and boss actor = $06AA (none); clear event_flags byte 0 (flags $00-$07 are scene-local), contact_lock, no_combat_scene, the PPU shadows and the colour buffer; LoadSceneAssets; if reload_menu_gfx is set, clear it and call RestoreSceneBgGfxAndPalette and LoadEquippedMagicGfx; BuildTileTypeMap; the map size in pages from MapPatchRectsAndMapSizes+$28/+$29 by location_id; InitActorPool; SpawnSceneActors; the map patches (code_011395, code_0112F5, ApplyLairStatesToScene, code_011445, code_0114D0, code_0114E4, ApplyFlagMapPatches); ClearBg3Buffer; ClearSwitchOwnersOnReturn; two RunActors passes; ApplyPlayerWeaponPose; RedrawBackgroundsAtEntry unless location_id is $10; vram_upload_flags bit 0; scene_variant and asset_skip_mask = 0; rng_state+1 = frame_counter (OQ-I013-1); joy_release_latch = $FFFF; frame_counter = $FFFF; window registers WH0 = 0 and WH1 = $FF; ResetSortBuckets; hud_dirty_flags = $1F unless event flag $FA ($1A7D bit 2).

=== NOTES ===
- ClearBg3Buffer (25 call sites: the front end, the scene init, the iris out) fills bg3_tilemap_buffer ($7F:7000, $1000 bytes) with $2000; the upload flag is the caller's business. ClearSwitchOwnersOnReturn zeroes switch_owner_table ($7F:0483, $400 bytes) only on a return trip (return_active non-zero).
- The transition and iris routines are JSR targets of ChangeSceneIfRequested and must stay in this block in this order: RunIrisTransition is reached by BRL from PlayTransitionOut and BMI from PlayTransitionIn, and ends with the RTS of the iris loop.
- Locations $0F-$12 have no HUD, no animated strip and no weapon pose; location $10 also skips the background redraw. $10-$12 run the reduced loop (OQ-I027-2).
lib_shared_027260:
Reset of the actor sort buckets (file offsets 160352-160374, SNES $04:F260-$F276, bank 04).

=== MODEL ===
ResetSortBuckets zeroes $0100-$02FF (256 bucket words) and writes the end marker $FFFF at $0300. The page is the bucket table of the actor sort (FillSortBuckets and FlattenSortBuckets in engine_scheduler_sprites_combat_collision); an empty table with the marker is the start state.

=== NOTES ===
- Callers: the end of LoadBootGraphicsBuffers and the end of InitSceneState.
- BuildTileTypeMap builds its metatile mask table in the same page ($0200-$02FF, FillTileTypeMap) during the scene load; ResetSortBuckets at the end of InitSceneState wipes it again.
- The writes are DBR-relative ($0100,X): they hit WRAM $0100 with the engine's DBR $01.
